text:
incident-bot: P1 — Elevated latency and increased 5xx rates observed in ap-southeast-1 impacting Hosted API and several Dedicated pools. Automated alerts triggered at 2025-11-02T02:07:14Z. Suspected AWS regional service degradation. See AWS status: https://status.aws.amazon.com/ — monitoring graphs attached (datadog link).
alex: paging oncall. I'm awake and looking. seeing 5xx spike at the edge + backend timeouts. hitting both hosted endpoints and customer-dedicated pools in ap-southeast-1.
carla: I'm taking incident commander. initial impact: error rate up ~12% 5xx on text-generation routes, median p50 latency doubled, p95 spiked to >2.5s. Dedicated pools in ap-southeast-1 showing queue growth and prewarm failures.
ingrid: Product — can we get a quick customer impact summary? Which customers are actively hitting Dedicated pools in the region? any legal/regulatory constraints for moving traffic?
jordan: Support — open tickets: 7 high-priority from customers A, B, and C complaining of timeouts. Customer B has a fallback region but saw rate-limit errors when we attempted cross-region routing. Adding notes to their tickets. Will merge status updates into status.redwood.ai once we have text.
tao: Infra — I'm seeing a cluster of AWS Control Plane API errors around the same time. A bunch of Describe/Attach calls are returning 5xx/503 and ELB target health checks are flapping. Could be a regional control-plane issue. Also seeing increased STS latency (token exchange) for instances in ap-southeast-1.
aws-support: AWS has posted an event for ap-southeast-1 (compute control plane and ELB) — engineers investigating. Reference: https://status.aws.amazon.com/incidents/ASD-2025-11-02-ap-southeast-1
alex: Immediate mitigations proposed:
- divert new Hosted API traffic away from ap-southeast-1 to fallback regions (eu-west-1 / us-east-1) via smart-routing policy
- fail Dedicated pools in region to secondary pools (if they have cross-region replication) or mark pools degraded and push customers to their reserved fallback
- reduce aggressive batching to lower backend pressure
- increase SDK/client retries with exponential backoff for internal calls
carla: Agreed. I'll run traffic steering. Tao, can you validate that rerouting won't blow through rate limits in fallback regions? Also prepare a canary of ~1% traffic to eu-west-1 first.
tao: On it. Running smoke canary now: `curl -H \"Authorization: Bearer <token>\" https://hosted-api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{\"prompt\":\"hi\"}' --resolve hosted-api.redwood.ai:443:3.125.45.11`
tao: Canary responses to eu-west-1 look fine, p95 ~120ms. Starting progressive shift of new traffic at 02:18Z with 1% -> 10% -> 50% target over next 20m.
ingrid: We need a short status snippet for customer-facing page. Drafting: "We are investigating elevated latency and errors for requests routed to ap-southeast-1. Engineers are routing traffic to alternate regions and monitoring. Some Dedicated customers in ap-southeast-1 may experience degraded throughput. Updates every 15 minutes." Thoughts?
jordan: That's good. Add note about support contact and that we're prioritizing customers with reserved capacity.
incident-bot: On-call handoff scheduled: alex -> tao at 02:35Z. Please ack when handoff complete.
alex: Handoff to tao acknowledged. I’m pausing page noise and switching to observer role.
tao: Took over as IC at 02:35Z. Current status: traffic steering at 60% away from ap-southeast-1. 5xx rate still elevated for remaining ~40% of traffic but trending down. AWS posted that they are seeing degraded ELB control plane in the region.
carla: We should also enable prefix KV cache hits serving stale cached completions for non-sensitive requests to reduce tail latency. Enabling cache-serving mode for hosted generation for 15m window now.
tao: Cache mode enabled. Also disabled continuous batching for ap-southeast-1 nodes to reduce head-of-line latencies.
aws-support: AWS update: root cause under investigation, engineers deploying mitigation. No ETA yet. We have Case ID: 9876543210 opened with AWS support.
jordan: Sending targeted customer updates to the 7 affected customers now (short, includes CAUTION note about potential data plane timeouts and suggested retrying).
ingrid: Are there observability blindspots? I saw Datadog metrics delayed ~2m for some traces — not sure if Datadog or AWS pushing logs slowly.
carla: Noted. We're switching to local aggregation / agent logs for critical traces and uploading after the window. Documenting in incident log.
alex: Quick note — rate limiting rules were catching some cross-region retries; temporarily relaxing token bucket thresholds in fallback regions to avoid throttling client retries.
tao: Completed full traffic shift for new requests at 02:55Z to target fallback regions for 90% of traffic. Remaining 10% are draining connections in ap-southeast-1 as we wait for AWS stabilization.
incident-bot: Pager silence set for non-p1 alerts for involved oncalls while incident active.
carla: Early impact summary for execs: ~14% of global traffic routed through ap-southeast-1 at peak; we observed a max 5xx rate of 12% in that region. After mitigations, global 5xx back to baseline ~1.2% and ap-southeast-1 residual 5xx ~2.8% (draining). No data loss. Several Dedicated customers experienced throughput degradation but failed over per policy.
jordan: Customers updated. No escalations to legal/compliance reported.
aws-support: AWS update 02:58Z: mitigation steps in place, error rates decreasing; detailed RCA will follow. We'll update the case and provide ETA for full recovery.
tao: Monitoring continues. I'll keep this thread as the primary coordination channel. Plan: hold incident until ap-southeast-1 5xx <0.5% for 30m and ELB/control-plane events cleared by AWS.
ingrid: Postmortem owners? Carla + tao to lead technical, Jordan to lead customer comms, Alex to review oncall runbook gaps.
carla: Postmortem checklist items: timeline, mitigation steps, why cross-region retry throttles were hit, caching as mitigation, whether autoscaler/reactive autoscaling made situation worse, update runbooks for immediate traffic steering.
alex: One action already: add automated reroute policy that triggers when regional control-plane errors exceed threshold for 5m (to avoid manual IC intervention). Creating a ticket in infra backlog.
tao: Noted. I'll keep watch and hand back to alex at 03:30Z if stable.
incident-bot: Incident status changed: monitoring -> assessing -> resolved_pending_wait (when criteria met). Updates every 15m.
carla: Final note for thread: thanks team. Good coordinated run. After AWS clears region, we'll perform controlled re-introduction of traffic and confirm no regression. I'll draft the customer-facing post-incident note once RCA available.
alex: Acknowledged. Handing back to alex at 03:30Z — tao -> alex handoff complete.
incident-bot: Thread closed for new pings at 03:48Z pending postmortem.
